findings.text: The first assertion of test_text_selection_skips_a_figure_only_record is vacuous: the figure-only record is written under project['tmp_path'] / 'figure-only-store', but select_review_for_head reads the default store root, so actual is None whether or not the skip exists and the assertion does not exercise the guard it was added for. The monkeypatched second half (:353) does exercise it, and the declared negative control reddens on that half, so the guard is still covered.

findings.evidence: read reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:331-334 against the node id shape minted at reckon/crew/repair.py:314-328.
findings.text: _review_in_flight distinguishes a figure review from a text review by testing whether the live pointer's node id ends with '-figure' rather than reading the review's stored rubric. A run whose id (with no head suffix) ends in '-figure' would mint a text-review node id with the same suffix and be misclassified; the discriminator is a name heuristic where the pointer already carries the rubric through the record.

findings.evidence: read reckon/crew_dispatch_commands.py:2485-2492; the file is not among the node's declared write paths.
findings.text: The printed review-missing command previews only the text brief (recovery._review_dispatch_fields(subject, write=False)['brief_text']), so for a run whose commits change a figure the printed command does not name the figure review, its rubric, or its own record paths, even though a real dispatch now composes all three. The node could not touch this file (outside its declared write paths), so it is recorded rather than repaired.
